# Results — Study 90 (Weekend / day-of-week effect) on the real total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — measure the
**per-weekday mean daily return** on **total-return** SPY, the **Monday-vs-rest** and
**Tuesday-vs-rest** contrasts with HAC *t*-stats, a **pre-2000 vs post-2000** split *with a
test of the change*, and a literal **"buy Tuesday" / "skip Monday"** timer net of **1 bp**
per switch against buy-and-hold. Day-of-week is calendar-known, so there is **no execution
lag**. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY (total return) | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |

## Per-weekday mean daily return (whole sample)

| Weekday | Mean (bps) | n | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Mon | **+5.64** | 1,578 | +2.06 |
| **Tue** | **+7.17** | 1,725 | **+2.64** |
| Wed | +6.20 | 1,723 | +2.21 |
| Thu | +1.46 | 1,690 | +0.52 |
| Fri | +3.32 | 1,683 | +1.33 |

> **Monday is *positive* on this tape** — there is no negative-Monday "weekend effect" in the
> SPY era. Tuesday is the strongest single weekday, but that is the only thing the folklore
> got directionally right.

## The two headline contrasts (whole sample)

| Contrast | Difference (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| Monday − rest | +1.08 | +0.36 |
| Tuesday − rest | +3.03 | +1.00 |

Neither clears |*t*| = 2. The Monday effect (claimed negative) is not even the right sign;
the Tuesday tilt is the right sign but not statistically distinguishable from the other days.

## Pre-2000 vs post-2000 — with a HAC test of the *change*

| Effect | Pre-2000 (bps) | Post-2000 (bps) | Change (bps) | HAC *t* (change) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Monday − rest | +4.78 | +0.09 | −4.69 | −0.77 |
| Tuesday − rest | +1.77 | +3.36 | +1.59 | +0.23 |

The Monday contrast is *positive in both halves* (the negative-Monday effect is absent across
the whole SPY record, not just decayed), and the change across the split is not significant
(|*t*| < 2 for both) — we cannot certify a "decay" because there was no significant effect
here to decay from.

## The literal timers — net of 1 bp/switch

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Time in mkt | Switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy Tuesday only | **2.36%** | 8.4% | **0.320** | −37.4% | 21% | 3,450 |
| Skip Monday | 7.30% | 16.4% | 0.512 | −48.9% | 81% | 3,155 |
| Buy & hold | **10.82%** | 18.6% | **0.646** | −55.2% | 100% | 0 |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is Monday negative (the weekend effect)? | **No** — Monday is **+5.64 bps**, Monday−rest **+1.08 bps** (HAC *t* +0.36) |
| Does Tuesday beat the other days? | Directionally yes (**+3.03 bps**) but **not significantly** (HAC *t* +1.00) |
| Did the (absent) Monday effect "decay" post-2000? | Change **−4.69 bps**, HAC *t* **−0.77** — not significant |
| Buy-Tuesday CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **−8.46 pts/yr** (2.36% vs 10.82%) |
| Skip-Monday CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **−3.52 pts/yr** (7.30% vs 10.82%) |
| Buy-Tuesday / Skip-Monday Sharpe vs buy-and-hold | **−0.326 / −0.133** (both worse) |

## How to read it

- **Signal → WEAK.** Tuesday is the strongest weekday and clears |*t*| = 2 on its *own* mean
  (+2.64), but the *claim* — a difference vs the other days — does **not** (Tuesday−rest *t*
  = +1.00), and the Monday claim is the wrong sign entirely. With five weekday tests in play,
  no contrast survives honestly. The literature says real (1953–1977); this SPY tape alone
  can't certify it.
- **Tradability → MIRAGE.** Every literal rule loses badly: "buy Tuesday" earns **8.5 pts/yr
  less** than buy-and-hold (you sit in cash 79% of the time and forfeit the equity premium);
  "skip Monday" loses 3.5 pts/yr. The weekday tilt, even taken at face value, is dwarfed by
  the lost beta.
- **Weekend effect still there? → BUSTED.** The defining feature — a *negative* Monday — is
  absent across the entire SPY record (Monday is positive pre- and post-2000), and the
  change-across-2000 test is insignificant. The famous effect lived in the pre-ETF era French
  studied; it is not in this tape.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tape (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative control
```
